AOC w/Axelrod tells a story she said she's not sure she shared before: In her first orientation in Congress, Joe Crowley, the Dem she beat, was up speaking and was clearly well liked by his colleagues.
"A congressman leans over to me and says: 'Man, it’s such a shame that girl beat him.”
"I looked back at him and said: 'you mean me?'”



— https://nitter.net/natashakorecki/status/2052882561030905871#m
Ted Turner Told Us This Would Happen - Playboy playboy.com/read/politics/te…

8 days after Supreme Court weakens Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, Republicans in Tennessee vote to redraw Congressional lines in order to dilute the vote in Memphis - the nation's largest majority-black city - and eliminate the state's only Dem congressional seat nytimes.com/2026/05/07/us/el…

a few notes (from someone who was heavy in very serious journalism awards circuit around this time).  1. Despite the universal praise now, I heard this criticism of Julie Brown's reporting a lot from very serious big deal journalists. For ex, a WaPo "senior editor" once dismissed her 2018 work as not having anything new compared to his own work (which...didn't move the Epstein story forward at all) 2. Big Journalism Awards Inc is over-indexed on "newness" which penalizes work over multi years (a

There was also the time WaPo won the Pulitzer for coverage of Trump/Russia/Sessions etc. WaPo's work was, objectively, more consequential. The decision was made. Convo closed. Then NYT launched a campaign and got the decision overturned and turned into a "co-winner" situation

The reason any of us know about the 1921 Tulsa Massacre is due to decades of work by many people. No one is more responsible than Don Ross: 
As a high school student, in 1971, he began documenting oral histories and other accounts of the destruction of Black Wall Street. He was lead organizer of public events commemorating the 75 anniversary, in 1996, which created the first memorial in Greenwood. He authored and championed the legislation creating a state commission to reinvestigate what happen

"...what happens if a memory you have held for years, one that has proved consequential to how you view yourself or others, turns out to be false? Or, at the very least, only part of the story?" bostonglobe.com/2026/05/05/o…

He spent 60 years building Black political power. He sees a wipeout coming: Press Robinson was the first member of his family to vote and the first Black person to win a seat on the Baton Rouge school board. He thinks a Supreme Court ruling will erase political gains African Americans have made across the South. wapo.st/4ukcV1b

never knew this ‘68 subplot: Ronald Smothers, more or less kept Stokely Carmichael out of prison through accurate reporting contradicting an unbylined NYT’s account claiming Stokely told people to get guns. Smothers captured Stokely saying the opposite nytimes.com/2026/05/03/us/ro…

“Of the 250 years since the country’s founding, less than a quarter unfolded under the aegis of universal suffrage. Color television, credit cards, and Barbie dolls arrived earlier than the VRA and will survive longer.” theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/0…
